To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

honeybee colonies can survive in landscapes with poor overall foraging conditions, as long as the foraging distance and the timing of foraging gaps are not too high, and that the mechanisms behind colony failure are mainly driven by a reduction of the queen's egg-lay, and the resulting lack of workforce for brood care and reduced workforce for foraging.

(1) the effects of forage availability on honeybee colonies depend strongly on the timing of foraging gaps; (2) the effects of poor forage supply on colony survival depend on the foraging distance; (3) the effect of forage supply on the queen's reproductive capacity is the main factor driving colony extinction.

the effects of forage availability on honeybee colonies are complex.
forage stress can be a major factor in colony mortality, especially if forage gaps occur in July, when the queen's egg-larying rate is at its seasonal peak.
